source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT's Ashburn VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, 2.2 percent of Virginia's disclosed data center total, in a state where only 26 of 332 mapped facilities publish any capacity figure at all.

The 36 MW ranks 14th among those 26 disclosing Virginia facilities, which together account for 1,639.4 MW. That is a rank inside a self-selected minority, not inside the state's full data center stock. The building holds 125,000 square feet of technical space, which works out to about 288 watts per square foot. Ashburn is where most of Virginia's published capacity concentrates, so the site sits in the state's main hub rather than at its edge.

For AI, the published capacity converts into a bounded amount of hardware. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks, and at typical power ratios for large language model training that is roughly 1,100 to 1,400 accelerators. That is one building's worth of compute. It does not show how much of it runs training rather than inference or ordinary enterprise workloads.

The data does not cover what would decide the facility's role in AI scaling. The grid connection is not published. Whether the capacity is reserved for AI workloads is not published. No certifications are published, and no announced expansion is recorded, which is the single input missing from the suitability score of 68. The megawatt figure describes the building, not the power supply behind it.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
